sources.rights_notes: The Library of Congress summary identifies Theodore Hamilton Carr as an enlisted Army veteran, 1943-1945, and states that his biographical form records OSS attachment. The interview is used through short excerpts and project-authored paraphrase; no recording or transcript is republished.

organizations.normalization_notes: Military assignment is not counted as civilian employment.

affiliations.role_title: Enlisted Reserve radio trainee; active-duty Army service before OSS training
affiliations.date_precision: The Library of Congress service summary dates Army service from 1943. Carr recalled reserve enlistment, Milwaukee radio training, active service at Fort Sheridan, and transfer to Washington for OSS training before D-Day; the official Army file dates active entry to January 17, 1944.
affiliations.research_notes: Carr's own sequence establishes Army status immediately before OSS training. It is a military assignment, not civilian employment; the precise reserve-to-active-to-OSS dates still require Box 109.

affiliations.date_precision: Carr recalled that he had just finished high school and was 17 when he entered the Enlisted Reserve. The interview does not name the school or establish school employment.
affiliations.research_notes: This is student status directly before reserve service. It is kept separate from the later Army-to-OSS pathway and is not an employer claim.

claims.claim_text: Gene A. Carr is confirmed as the Army private whose official entry record matches the OSS index's restricted identifier; occupation value 706 is unassigned in the official code list and remains uninterpreted.
claims.evidence_paraphrase: The index and Army file agree on the exact name and restricted identifier. The Army record documents entry as a private on November 11, 1942; the official code list does not define value 706.
claims.identity_match_assessment: Confirmed by exact full-name and restricted-identifier agreement between two official records.
claims.temporal_assessment: The Army record establishes status and entry date but does not document when Carr entered OSS or identify a predecessor employer or occupation.
claims.match_notes: The restricted identifier is withheld. Undefined value 706 is not expanded or treated as evidence of employment.

claims.claim_text: Theodore H. Carr's immediate pre-OSS pathway was enlisted reserve and active-duty service in the United States Army before transfer to OSS training in Washington.
claims.evidence_excerpt: sent on down to Washington to the OSS training
claims.evidence_paraphrase: Carr described reserve enlistment, Army radio training, active service, and then transfer to Washington for OSS training before D-Day.
claims.identity_match_assessment: The person-specific Library of Congress collection is linked to the index by the official restricted-identifier match and corroborating Army service details.
claims.temporal_assessment: Carr explicitly narrates Army stages followed by OSS training, supporting an immediate military pathway but not a civilian employer.
claims.match_notes: Modeled as military_assignment. Exact reserve, active-duty, and OSS transfer dates remain for Box 109 review.
